scope: Current working tree; no engine runs; counts do not measure quality

identity.counting_note: object counts describe size, never quality
declared_changes: initial blockout: hierarchy, containment, connectivity, scale, spine

identity.counting_note: object counts describe size, never quality
declared_changes: added a covered gatehouse and two gallery arches as real thresholds, each darker than its neighbours, to answer the collapsed perceptual space
cut stair sectors from 16 to 10 and raised room sectors from 10 to 15
lowered the gallery from about 2.7 to about 2.0 player heights
gave the chapel two side aisles and a raised, brighter apse holding the switch
gave the crypt a larger hall plus a reliquary and a cistern chamber
declared the open exterior stairs as courtyard circulation instead of gallery
fixed probe:reach_crypt to open both sides of the crypt gate and reworded the ossuary probe so its intended answer is not phrased as a failure
surface treatment deliberately unchanged; that is iteration 2

identity.counting_note: object counts describe size, never quality
declared_changes: one dominant floor/ceiling/wall triple per assembly, each tile chosen from both mined corpus usage and its rendered appearance
ceilings picked for what they look like: 454 coffered over the nave, 4 light stone over the apse, 285 vault over the approach, 455 moss over the derelict gallery
courtyard wall changed from smooth marble 2490 to coursed rubble 110 so the wall carries a unit of scale
51 decoration sprites attached to architectural roles at precedent-anchored density
geometry and shading deliberately unchanged from v1 so any hierarchy movement would prove the critic was reading something other than what changed

identity.counting_note: object counts describe size, never quality
declared_changes: ceilings set from corpus percentiles for each space's footprint rather than from round multiples of player height: nave 7->10, aisles 4->6, apse 6->8, gallery 6->12, exit 4->8, ledge 4->6, gatehouse 3->5, crypt hall 2.18->5, arches 2->4
crypt cells deliberately kept near 3 player heights on the E6M3 precedent, as an argued exception rather than an unexamined default

chamfers and shallower non-45-degree facets on the courtyard, chapel mass, crypt hall, gallery, exit hall, ledge and crypt cells; the gatehouse splayed at 37 degrees; the apse made an eight-sided radial chancel; the garden bed made an octagonal planter
sprite repeats derived from each tile's pixel size and a stated target height in player heights, instead of copied from the campaign mode
the loop arch given the emblem its twin already had

identity.counting_note: object counts describe size, never quality
declared_changes: the garden bed raised 6144 above the courtyard instead of sunk 2048, and the chancel raised 6144 above the nave instead of 2048, so the level finally has one-way vertical relationships; v3 had none anywhere
a three-tread chancel stair beside a direct 6144 opening, so the chancel is reached without closing the view back down into the nave
the gallery ascent rise changed from 3840 to 4096, the rise the corpus uses for 771 of its 1283 stair rises
all four stairs written as bloodmap.vocabulary.staircase calls instead of hand-rolled loops that tracked their own previous edge
three wall niches written as bloodmap.vocabulary.recess calls, sized on the corpus profile: flush floor, lowered ceiling, a few percent of the host
a raised tomb block in the crypt hall: a third vertical relationship, and something for the level's second-largest interior to be about

identity.counting_note: object counts describe size, never quality
declared_changes: the crypt stops being one tile: the hall, its stair and the tomb block take E6M3's crypt treatments, tile 1097 stays only on the reliquary where the corpus supports it, and the two larger chambers take a third set
segmented arcs at the mined corpus parameters replace chamfers on the planter, the chancel, two courtyard corners, two crypt-hall corners and two gallery corners
the planter's eight hand-written connection edges are generated from its own outline, so its sixteen segments cannot drift out of step with its connections
four viewpoints declare an upward pitch, so the level's ceilings and its sky are looked at for the first time in five iterations

the sky panorama itself was a compiler fix rather than a source change: PlanarLayout now emits the sixteen-panel sky every campaign map with a parallax sector declares, instead of the single panel new_level hardcoded
